description: Result of work item WI-36, task 7: the suspected v1 bugs of work_items/phase3/README.md (Findings from the v1 code) confirmed or refuted by running the v1 code, further observations, and what the corpus shows. Every case id names an entry in tests/golden/expected; tests/golden/test_golden_format.py checks that the ids exist.

suspicions.suspicion: Function calls with arguments always fail (Code parser.ahk:594, inverted condition)
suspicions.detail: Every call with an argument: parse error 'Expecting punctuation: ")"'. Calls without arguments fail too, with 'Unexpected token in expression'. In script mode v1 ignores the parse error: 'x := round(2.5)' stores the text '02.5', 'foo(1)' reaches the evaluator ('unknown function foo called'). round, object and print can never be called in v1.

suspicions.suspicion: Escape sequences in strings are lost (:718 compares with the empty variable name)
suspicions.detail: The escape character (backtick) is dropped and the next character is kept: "a`nb" gives 'anb' (no linefeed), "a``b" gives 'ab'. An escaped quote ends in the error 'Linefeed inside a string'. A doubled quote "a""b" gives 'ab', not 'a"b'.

suspicions.suspicion: % (modulo) is not known to the evaluator
suspicions.detail: Evaluation error "Error: Can't apply operator %". The parser knows % (precedence 20), the evaluator does not.

suspicions.suspicion: ! and not at the start of an expression fail
suspicions.detail: '!' is a parse error at the start and after 'and' or '||'. 'not' does not fail but does not negate: at the start it is read as a variable named 'not' and concatenated (not 0 gives the text '0', not 'abc' gives 'abc'); after 'and' the value is wrong (1 and not 0 gives 0). Only as an operator behind an operand does it negate the right side (not not 1 gives 0: the first 'not' is a variable, the second the operator). Inside 'if', 'if not a' behaves like 'if a' (the body runs for a=1, not for a=0).
"a ;b" and a tab before the semicolon: parse error 'Linefeed inside a string'. "a;b" and "a;" are fine.

suspicions.suspicion: this.input.croak does not exist; errors are swallowed
suspicions.detail: 'else' without 'if': the parser records no error and skips the keyword; only the evaluator reports the unspecific 'Unexpected error during evaluation', and the next statement still runs.

suspicions.suspicion: The evaluator uses v1 operators: '' + 1 is '', 4/2 is 2.000000, < compares text alphabetically
suspicions.detail: '""+1' is the empty text, '4/2' is the number 2.000000. '"a"<"B"' is 1 (case-insensitive alphabetical), '"10"<"9"' is 0 (both look like numbers: numeric), '"10"<"9a"' is 1. '=' ignores case, '==' does not; case folding is ASCII only ('"ä"="Ä"' is 0).

suspicions.suspicion: The location of a variable follows from its name (Variables.ahk:219, :253)
suspicions.detail: A_ needs location thread or loop, other names never; the global_ / static_ prefix is compared case-insensitively; loop wins over thread; a variable with a global_ name in the instance store is invisible.

suspicions.suspicion: Hidden variables per scope; global and static are read from disk on every access
suspicions.verdict: not checked (hidden variables); disk access visible indirectly
suspicions.detail: The harness does not set hidden variables. Global values come back from the file as text (5, 0.500000); objects come back as objects.

suspicions.suspicion: Built-in variables: 55 from AHK and 14 of its own
suspicions.detail: Fixed-value built-ins and 29 machine- or time-dependent ones (volatile, only the type is stored) are covered. a_vt, A_VerticalTab, a_ff, A_Formfeed are handled by BuiltInVariable_Get but are in neither name list, so the variable does not exist and the value is empty.

observations.detail: A value that went through Var_Get (it returns a clone) is a text in v1, even if it was a number before (stored 0.5 reads 0.500000). Only the result of arithmetic is a pure number. Global and static variables come back from their file as text.

2*-3 becomes the unknown operator '*-': the right operand is silently dropped and the result is 2. Same for 5--3 (5), 7/-2 (7), -8/-2 (-8), 7//-2, 1<>2 (1). With a space (5 - -3) it works. The corpus has no such value.

observations.topic: Unary minus only in front of a number literal
Division by zero and integer division
observations.detail: Division by zero gives the empty text, no error. // truncates towards zero for negative integers (-7//2 is -3) and gives the float format for floats (7.0//2 is 3.000000).
Floats have 6 decimals (0.1+0.2 is 0.300000), also for big values (333333333333.333313). Integers wrap at 64 bit. '0x10'+0 is 16; '1e3'+0 and '5abc'+1 are empty.

The parser never ends (the harness stops it after 8 s, outcome timeout) for a script line that starts with ';', for an unknown character at the start of a statement, and for the assignment operators //=, ^=, %= in script mode. As an expression the same operators are an unknown operator: the right operand is dropped and the result is the left value ('x //= 2' returns x, nothing is assigned).

observations.topic: Paths into objects: readable, not writable
observations.detail: Var_Set calls Var_CheckName, which refuses a dot, so 'a.b := 5' only logs f0 'Setting variable a.b failed. It contains forbidden characters.' and changes nothing. Whole objects can be assigned.

observations.topic: Dereferences in names do not work
observations.detail: '%' starts an operator token, so a%i% and %n% give parse errors or "Can't apply operator %".

observations.topic: Paths into global and static objects
observations.detail: global_o.a is empty: the existence check looks for a file global_o.a.ahfvd.

observations.topic: Objects: key case, integer keys, order, JSON text
observations.detail: Keys are case-insensitive (c and C are one key, the spelling of the first insertion is kept). A key that looks like an integer is an integer ('01' and '1' are the same key, the later value wins). Enumeration order: integers ascending, then text sorted case-insensitively. liste.1, liste[1] and liste["1"] are the same; index 0 and out-of-range read empty. The JSON text of an object (ConvertObjectToString) is indented by 2 spaces and escapes / as \/; a float inside an object comes out as text.

observations.topic: An assignment has no value, no short circuit
observations.detail: Var_Set returns nothing, so '(x := 3) + 1' is not a sum, 'x := y := 3' is an error, and 'x := (y := 3)' stores the empty text in x. 'and' and 'or' evaluate both sides: '0 and (x := 5)' still sets x.

observations.topic: A_ names cannot be set without a location
observations.detail: Setting an A_ name from a script logs f0 'No permission.'. Reading an unknown A_ name gives the empty text and only the f0 log 'Retrieving variable ... failed'.

Refused: empty (Empty), a leading digit (StartsWithNumber, also 1.5), and every character the interpreter rejects in 'asdf%name%' (space, dot, minus, comma, semicolon, colon, brackets, question mark, parenthesis, quote, percent, backtick, operators, control characters) and names longer than 253 characters. Accepted: letters including umlauts, digits, underscore, @, $, #, emoji, and reserved words (if, A_Index).

A parse error in a script is not looked at by var_evaluateScript; the evaluator runs anyway (outcomes parse_error_ignored / eval_error). if works without braces for one statement, with else, else if and nesting. A statement that is not a name (1 + 1, "abc") is an error; two assignments on one line fail; there is no line continuation.

corpus.source: the 22 example flows of v1/AppData/Saved Flows (group corpus_flows)
not_used: operators glued to a minus sign
corpus.failing_in_v1: One distinct value, %a_windowID% run as an expression (3 cases). It is a parameter whose content type could not be determined, so it also runs as a substitution, where it works. All other expressions, substitutions and names run without a parser or evaluator error: real flows use the part of the language that works (comparisons, and/or, literals, variable reads, read-only paths).
corpus.note: The variants give every variable a distinct small number or a t<n> text, so most conditions evaluate to 0. They check the type handling, not every branch; the hand-written groups cover the branches.

not_covered: evalparam (x_AutoEvaluateOneParameter) is not in the harness: it lives in the API file next to about a hundred functions that need the whole application, and #Include cannot take one function. Options if WI-42 wants golden data for the post-checks: a copy in the harness (no longer v1 code) or stubs for all callees. Decision needed then.

The editor/manager variants xx_replaceVariables, xx_EvaluateExpression, xx_CheckVariableName in v1/Source_Common/Multithreading/API for Elements.ahk pass the variables String, pars, VarName (empty there; the parameters are called p_String ...): read from the source, not executed. The cases with common=true test the _Common functions themselves.
Hidden variables, the loop-variable stack, Var_GetListOf*, deleting variables.
lang() is a stand-in that fills in the numbered arguments; error texts read 'line 1, col 4'. The real texts depend on the UI language.
The path through which an element reaches the evaluator (x_AutoEvaluateParameters) was read, not run.
